## Research

My work spans three intersecting areas.

::: research-grid
### Science, communication, and society

Scientist climate advocacy and activism, and questions of credibility and public trust.

### Collective climate action

Collective action from the perspective of those taking part, and public responses to climate protest and civil disobedience.

### Institutional climate responses

Institutional climate responses and leadership. My work at Lancaster University, supported by the Wellcome Trust, explores the ethical and cultural dimensions of sustainability in UK higher education, including how universities conceptualise their responsibilities in addressing the climate crisis.
:::

I use mixed methods, spanning ethnography, interviews, surveys, experiments, media analysis, and video-based behavioural analysis, to understand both the psychological processes and the real-world behaviours underpinning social change. My work combines ethnographic depth with psychological theory and behavioural data. [How I approach research](approach.qmd){.more-link}

## Background

I have held senior research roles at the University of Bristol, where I worked across the Schools of Psychology and Policy Studies researching public attitudes to disruptive climate protest, and at Lancaster University, where I am based in the Social Processes Group within the Department of Psychology, conducting research on scientist advocacy and activism, research culture, and universities' climate responses. These positions have allowed me to combine interdisciplinary research, applied policy engagement, and collaborative projects with academic and non-academic partners. I trained in anthropology (BA, MA), cognitive science (MSc), and social psychology (PhD).
